newsitem.title: ANGOLA: ANGOLANS NATIONAL BANK DEVALUES CURRENCY.
newsitem.headline: ANGOLANS NATIONAL BANK DEVALUES CURRENCY.

text.p: Angola's central bank has devalued the currency, the Angolan press reported Tuesday.
"Banco National de Angola (BNA) has decided to devalue the national currency, the Kwanza, from 203,000 to the U.S. dollar to 265,600," Journal de Angola, a Luanda daily, reported.
The BNA rate has remained virtually unchanged for a year.
The country's black market rate has risen steadily in the past two weeks. Today the black market rate in Luanda stands at 300,000 Kwanzas to the dollar.
Economists say there are several reasons for devaluation.
"The banks are short of hard currency at the moment," said one Western economist. "This has led to a serious devaluation of the Kwanza, first on the black market, and now with the BNA."
Economists say about two weeks ago the government began allowing private businesses to import goods into Angola with their own money without going through the BNA, as had been required previously.
Businesses started buying heavily on the black market, pushing the value of the Kwanza down.

Other economists say in the past few weeks the government has also started paying months of back salaries to civil servants and buying arms, using up hard currency and causing a further devaluation of the currency.
